arxiv-2206-13217.title: Center-Embedding and Constituency in the Brain and a New Characterization of Context-Free Languages
arxiv-2206-13217.creator: Daniel Mitropolsky, Adiba Ejaz, Mirah Shi, Mihalis Yannakakis, Christos H. Papadimitriou
arxiv-2206-13217.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Daniel Mitropolsky, Adiba Ejaz, Mirah Shi, Mihalis Yannakakis, Christos H. Papadimitriou. A computational system implemented exclusively through the spiking of neurons was recently shown capable of syntax, that is, of carrying out the dependency parsing of simple English sentences. We address two of the most important questions left open by that work: constituency (the identification of key parts of the sentence such as the verb phrase) and the processing of dependent sentences, especially center-embedded ones.

arxiv-2208-06903.title: BRST Symmetry and the Convolutional Double Copy
arxiv-2208-06903.creator: Mahdi Godazgar
arxiv-2208-06903.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mahdi Godazgar. Motivated by the results of Anastasiou et al., we consider the convolutional double copy for BRST and anti-BRST covariant formulations of gravitational and gauge theories in more detail. We give a general BRST and anti-BRST invariant formulation of linearised 𝒩 = 0 \mathcal{N}=0 supergravity using superspace methods and show how this may be obtained from the square of linearised Yang-Mills theories. We demonstrate this relation for the Schwarzschild black hole and the ten-dimensional black string solution as two concrete examples.

arxiv-2304-01846.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by José D. Alvarado, Yoshiharu Kohayakawa, Patrick Morris, Guilherme O. Mota. The celebrated canonical Ramsey theorem of Erdős and Rado implies that for a given k k -uniform hypergraph (or k k -graph) H H , if n n is sufficiently large then any colouring of the edges of the complete k k -graph K n ( k ) K^{(k)}_{n} gives rise to copies of H H that exhibit certain colour patterns.

arxiv-2310-17279.title: Automatic Logical Forms improve fidelity in Table-to-Text generation
arxiv-2310-17279.creator: Iñigo Alonso, Eneko Agirre
arxiv-2310-17279.description: Abstract Table-to-text systems generate natural language statements from structured data like tables. While end-to-end techniques suffer from low factual correctness (fidelity), a previous study reported fidelity gains when using manually produced graphs that represent the content and semantics of the target text called Logical Forms (LF).

arxiv-2312-03416.title: Viscous rebound of a quasi-2D cylinder on a solid wall
arxiv-2312-03416.creator: Alicia Aguilar-Corona, Micheline Abbas, Matthieu J. Mercier, Laurent Lacaze
arxiv-2312-03416.description: Abstract 1 Abstract The purpose of the present study is to extend the simple concept of apparent coefficient of restitution, widely approached in the literature for the case of a single-contact-point between a sphere and a wall, to the case of bouncing whose complexity is increased due to the shape of the contacting object.

arxiv-2502-09198.title: Understanding High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization
arxiv-2502-09198.creator: Leonard Papenmeier, Matthias Poloczek, Luigi Nardi
arxiv-2502-09198.description: Abstract Recent work reported that simple BO ( BO ) methods perform well for high-dimensional real-world tasks, seemingly contradicting prior work and tribal knowledge. This paper investigates why. We identify underlying challenges that arise in high-dimensional BO and explain why recent methods succeed.

arxiv-2503-10089.title: Non-perturbative quarkonium dissociation rates in strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma
arxiv-2503-10089.creator: Biaogang Wu, Zhanduo Tang, Ralf Rapp
arxiv-2503-10089.description: Abstract Heavy quarks and quarkonia are versatile probes of the transport properties of the hot QCD medium produced in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions (URHICs). A robust description of heavy-flavor transport coefficients requires a microscopic approach that treats the open and hidden heavy-flavor sectors on the same footing.

arxiv-2505-13767.title: Dark States of Light and the Hidden Energy in Thermal Radiation Detection
arxiv-2505-13767.creator: Celso Jorge Villas-Boas, Ciro Micheletti Diniz
arxiv-2505-13767.description: Abstract We develop a quantum-optical framework demonstrating that thermal radiation can confine a significant portion of its energy in dark collective modes – highly entangled photon states that, despite their photonic nature, remain decoupled from matter through standard electromagnetic interactions.

pmc-11403961.title: Technical considerations for placental tissue processing and the subsequent impact on genome-wide DNA methylation analysis
pmc-11403961.creator: Kristen M Kocher, Julius Ngwa, Kushal J Kapse, Surajit Bhattacharya, Christopher Rossi, Emmanuele Delot, Adre duPlessis, Catherine Limperopoulos, Nickie Andescavage
pmc-11403961.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). To assess the impact of postnatal processing on placental DNA methylation, array data from flash-frozen placental tissue was compared to perfluorocarbon-immersed and formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded placental tissue. We observed that tissue exposed to perfluorocarbon showed no significant DNA methylation differences when compared to unprocessed tissue, while formalin processing altered the quality and reliability of the data produced on the DNA methylation array platform. Placental DNA methylation allows for the study of gene–environment interactions that influence the fetal environment and development.

pmc-11517170.title: Health promotion interventions for children and adolescents using e-health: a systematic review
pmc-11517170.creator: E Bae, M Jang
pmc-11517170.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe utilization of e-health in healthcare interventions has become increasingly prevalent due to its cost-effectiveness. Nevertheless, there is a paucity of evidence regarding the use of e-health in children, as the majority of e-health interventions are focused on adults. This study aimed to identify the components and effects of e-health intervention for the promotion of children’s health and to suggest strategies for their implementation.MethodsA systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines.

pmc-11642317.title: Development and Initial Outcomes of the Interdisciplinary ‘Early Identification and Intervention for Infants Network’ (Ei3) in Los Angeles
pmc-11642317.creator: Christiana D Butera, Amy Yeh, Manoj Biniwale, Edward Bloch, Debi Craddock, Mary Doyle, Sai N Iyer, Kari S Kretch, Nora Liu, Christine B Mirzaian, Barbara Sargent, Priscilla Solano, Margaret Swaine, Stacey C Dusing, Lindsay A Farrer
pmc-11642317.description: Background/Objectives: The Early Identification and Intervention for Infants (Ei3) Network is an interdisciplinary team dedicated to improving early detection and intervention of cerebral palsy (CP) in California. This paper describes the key (1) awareness-building and (2) capacity-building strategies utilized by the Ei3 Network in the first two years.

pmc-11657870.title: Reduced plastid genomes of colorless facultative pathogens Prototheca (Chlorophyta) are retained for membrane transport genes
pmc-11657870.creator: Kacper Maciszewski, Gabriela Wilga, Tomasz Jagielski, Zofia Bakuła, Jan Gawor, Robert Gromadka, Anna Karnkowska
pmc-11657870.description: BackgroundPlastids are usually involved in photosynthesis, but the secondary loss of this function is a widespread phenomenon in various lineages of algae and plants. In addition to the loss of genes associated with photosynthesis, the plastid genomes of colorless algae are frequently reduced further.

pmc-11691256.title: HOME HEALTH USE BY OLDER ADULTS WITH DEMENTIA: COMPARING MEDICARE ADVANTAGE AND TRADITIONAL MEDICARE
pmc-11691256.creator: Jamie Smith, Jianhui (Frank) Xu, Teneil Brown, Julia Burgdorf, Daniel Polsky, Katherine Ornstein
pmc-11691256.description: Skilled home health care (HHC) is a critical service for community-dwelling older adults with dementia, but the majority of evidence about its use and quality is based on Traditional Medicare (TM) beneficiaries. Medicare Advantage (MA) plans - which now enroll over half of Medicare beneficiaries - have flexibility in financing and managing HHC, potentially affecting access and utilization.

pmc-11957376.title: Environmental Cues Facilitate Maturation and Patterning of Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Cardiomyocytes
pmc-11957376.creator: Enrique Coca, Scott Cho, Christopher Kauffman, Alonzo D. Cook, Martin Tristani-Firouzi, Natalia S. Torres
pmc-11957376.description: Background/Aims:Advances in induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technology allow for reprogramming of adult somatic cells into stem cells from which patient- and disease-specific cardiomyocytes (CMs) can be derived. Yet, the potential of iPSC technology to revolutionize cardiovascular research is limited, in part, by the embryonic nature of these cells.

pmc-13019094.title: One-year changes in body composition and phase angle during feminizing gender-affirming hormone therapy: a longitudinal and comparative study
pmc-13019094.creator: Suna Avcı, Zehra Kara, Emre Durcan, Özge Polat Korkmaz, Ali Kimiaei, Seyedehtina Safaei, Şenol Turan, Alper Döventaş, Deniz Suna Erdinçler, Pınar Kadioglu
pmc-13019094.description: BackgroundGender dysphoria (GD) refers to the clinically significant distress or discomfort that may arise from a marked incongruence between an individual’s gender identity and the sex assigned at birth, involving primary and/or secondary sex characteristics and social roles. Gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) aims to alleviate this distress by aligning secondary sex characteristics with gender identity and improving psychological well-being.

pmc-13158249.title: Disturbance-mediated apparent competition across boreal landscapes: the role of primary productivity
pmc-13158249.creator: Branden T Neufeld, Clara Superbie, Cheryl A Johnson, Daniel Fortin, Philip D McLoughlin
pmc-13158249.description: ContextDisturbance-mediated apparent competition (DMAC) links landscape disturbance, alternative prey, and predator dynamics in ways that can reduce caribou recruitment and survival. Although DMAC underpins national recovery planning for boreal caribou (Rangifer tarandus caribou), its mechanisms have been evaluated mainly in southern, more productive forests.

pmc-13256008.title: Alcohol consumption and risk of atrial fibrillation: a pairwise and network meta-analysis
pmc-13256008.creator: Zain Ul Abideen Asad, Ali Haider Jafry, Usman Akbar, Christopher Beard, Jehanzeb Ahmed Khan, Satyam Krishan, Muhammad Hurera, Syeda Maheen Raza, Shari Clifton, Jessica Reese, Safi U Khan, Rakesh Gopinathannair, Estelle Torbey, Sunny S Po, Usman Baber, Stavros Stavrakis, Prashanthan Sanders
pmc-13256008.description: AimsDespite well-established evidence linking alcohol consumption to an increased risk of atrial fibrillation (AF), a clear threshold for safe intake remains undefined. Most clinical guidelines recommend abstinence or moderation, but lack specificity regarding quantitative limits and evidence-based thresholds for primary prevention of AF.

pmc-13389726.title: Community care for individuals with borderline personality disorder in Japan: a narrative review
pmc-13389726.creator: Miwa Sasaki
pmc-13389726.description: Objective: To synthesize Japanese literature on community care for individuals with borderline personality disorder (BPD) and identify key providers, care settings, support components, and implementation challenges to inform primary care involvement in community BPD care.Methods: We searched the Ichushi-Web and CiNii Research databases for Japanese-language publications on community-based care for individuals with BPD in Japan indexed through December 2025.

pmc-13602979.title: Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine Special Statement: Checklists for persons with sickle cell disease in pregnancy

pmc-13602979.description: This article presents checklists designed to guide clinicians in the comprehensive management of pregnant individuals with sickle cell disease, including prepregnancy, antepartum, delivery, and postpartum care, as well as the specific management of vaso‐occlusive crises. The checklists aim to standardize care, enhance documentation and communication, and improve maternal and neonatal outcomes.
